title: Heatmap
description: A grid of cells colored by value, over categories or numbers on both axes: activity by weekday and hour, correlation matrices, maps of a measure. Hover a cell to lift it, highlight its row and column and mark its value on the color legend.

examples.title: Contribution calendar
examples.description: A year of daily contributions like a GitHub profile: weeks as numeric columns, weekdays as rows, an x format that turns the week number into its month, and palette={["var(--success-color)"]} for a green ramp that reads well in light and dark themes.

examples.title: Weekly activity
examples.description: 7 × 24 cells over category axes. The default ramp is perceptual (OKLab) and follows the theme: from a near-white tint to a deep primary color in light mode, from a tint of the surface to a bright one in dark mode; the color legend shows its range. yCategories lists the rows from bottom to top, hence the reversed weekdays.

examples.title: Diverging scale
examples.description: colorScale lists the colors from the lowest to the highest value and accepts CSS variables, so the middle stop follows the theme. A symmetric valueRange keeps 0 in the middle of the scale.

examples.title: Confusion matrix
examples.description: Predictions of an image classifier, each cell colored by its share of the actual class. renderTooltip finds the hovered cell from item.index to show its count, and the recall and precision on the diagonal.

examples.title: Click a cell
examples.description: Conversion rate by traffic source and device. onPointClick gives item.index, the index of the clicked cell in data, which leads back to its sessions and orders for the readout; onPlotClick clears it.

examples.title: Correlation matrix
examples.description: Pairwise correlations of product metrics with colorScale="diverging": the danger color below colorMidpoint (0), the primary color above, a neutral middle that follows the theme; the same translated names are used for both axes.

examples.title: 20,000 cells
examples.description: A 200 × 100 grid with numbers on both axes. interaction={{ zoom: "xy" }} enables zooming (off by default for heatmaps): Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel, drag to pan, double-click to reset.

examples.title: Live sensor grid
examples.description: Inlet temperatures of the sensors of a server aisle, refreshed by a setInterval cleared on pause and unmount. A fixed valueRange keeps the same color for the same temperature at every refresh, and colorScale goes through theme colors from cool to hot.

examples.title: Cohort retention
examples.description: Share of each monthly signup cohort still active after N months: null values leave the future cells empty, which draws the classic triangle.

examples.title: Switching metrics
examples.description: Revenue, growth and margin by region and quarter: each metric brings its own colorScale (sequential, diverging around zero or a custom list), valueRange and format, switched with a RadioGroup.

color-scale.title: Diverging color scale
color-scale.description: A correlation matrix on a fixed -1 to 1 range: blue for negative values, red for positive ones, rounded cells.

props.valueName: Name of the value in the tooltip
props.height: Height of the chart, the legend included: pixels or any CSS length
props.options: Other engine options (axes, legend, tooltip, palette, format…) merged with the element's own properties; property only
props.instance: The engine instance (minerva-design/charts/core), null until the element is rendered and connected

events.minerva-hover: The hovered (or keyboard-focused) points changed; detail: { x, xLabel, items }, null when nothing is hovered
events.minerva-point-click: A point or a bar was clicked; detail: { x, xLabel, items }
events.minerva-plot-click: The plot area was clicked where there is no point; detail: { x, y } in data coordinates
events.minerva-zoom: The user zoomed or panned; detail: { x, y } (the visible ranges)
events.minerva-renderer-change: The backend is ready, or fell back after a GPU loss; detail: { renderer }

methods.getView: Visible range, null before the engine is created
methods.getRenderer: Backend in use (webgpu, webgl2, webgl, canvas2d), null until ready
